Keywords.Definition: If a card directly contradicts this reference, the card takes precedence.
If an effect states a figure cannot do something, that restriction overrides an effect that would allow it.
The active Hero resolves their simultaneous effects in the order they choose; Enemy effects resolve in Scenario/AI order.
If no duration is listed, the effect resolves immediately and ends.
Different effects stack unless stated otherwise. Multiple copies of the same named effect do not stack unless specifically allowed.
Deal damage to a target using a weapon, skill, or ability.
The standard attack printed on a Hero or Enemy card; unless otherwise stated it targets one enemy and grants no additional effects.
A primary activity during a Hero turn.
A card played outside your turn when its trigger occurs; it does not use an Action unless stated.
A card or ability that may be played without using an Action.
Reduce the next instance of damage you would take by 2, then remove Guard; does not stack unless stated.
Melee targeting beyond normal current-Location range as defined by the card; current system uses Location connections, not grid spaces.
Forced movement moves a figure to a legal connected revealed Location in the indicated direction/context; forced movement ignores Engagement unless stated.
Cannot be Pushed, Pulled, or otherwise forcibly moved.
Lose 1 Health at the specified trigger; final timing should follow System 008 once reconciled.
Ongoing Fire damage until removed/extinguished; final timing should follow System 008 once reconciled.
Cannot recover Health until removed, unless the final System 008 definition supersedes this entry.
-1 Attack.
Cannot perform an Action/activation as specified by the finalized Condition rules.
Cannot voluntarily Move; may perform other Actions.
Cannot be targeted by attacks unless attacker is in same Location or another rule allows it; removed by attacking or specified effects.
+1 Attack until removed unless a card states another duration.
Fighter resource; maximum 3. Earned/spent as specified by Fighter cards.
Cleric resource concept from earlier rules; Sister Elara's current deck primarily uses Consecrated/Inspired rather than explicit Faith costs.
Wizard cards gain their listed Arcane bonus while Vaelis occupies an Arcane Location.
A magical Location created by Wizard abilities. It has no inherent effect; Arcane cards gain listed bonuses while the Hero occupies one.
A blessed Location created by Cleric abilities. It has no inherent effect; cards referencing Consecrated gain listed bonuses.
High Health front-line combatant.
Long-range attacker with lower durability.
Fast enemy that targets isolated Heroes.
Manipulates terrain, conditions, or Hero positioning.
High movement with charge-style attacks.
Heals or enhances allies.
Creates additional enemies or battlefield objects.
Powerful non-boss enemy with unique abilities.
Major enemy with multiple abilities and higher durability.
Protect a unit until it reaches its destination.
Prevent enemies from occupying an objective for the required duration.
Move all surviving Heroes to the designated exit.
Remain alive until the specified round or event.
The equipped Weapon's Attack Bonus added to the Hero's Attack Value.
Reduces incoming damage. Damage = Attack − Armor.
Roll 1d6 + Weapon + modifiers. Attacks automatically hit.
A random travel challenge resolved by drawing from the Encounter Deck and rolling Encounter Severity.
Roll 1d6 plus current World Event modifiers, then resolve the drawn Encounter card's 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, or 7+ result.
The deck of random travel encounters used between or during quests when a rule instructs Heroes to resolve a Travel Encounter.
Spend 1 Action to draw and resolve the top valid card of the Exploration Deck while occupying a revealed Location, unless another effect changes the cost.
The deck used whenever a Hero Explores. Exploration cards may provide discoveries, opportunities, hazards, encounters, NPCs, story effects, or rewards.
An Exploration card is valid if its Terrain is Any, Any Outdoor, or matches the current Location's Terrain, Traits, Keywords, or Location Type. Invalid cards are discarded and another card is drawn.
An Explore instructed by a card, ability, Quest, or other effect without an Action cost resolves without spending an Action.
The deck of tangible items gained from Exploration, Encounters, Quests, enemies, and other rewards. Gold is tracked separately.
A Loot card used for a one-time effect. After its effect resolves, discard it unless the card states otherwise.
A tag describing thematic sources for Loot, such as Goblin, Forest, Cave, Settlement, or Quest. Effects may request Loot with a specific Drop Tag.
A formula listing the Materials, Tool, Craft Time, Gold Cost, Result, and unlock requirement needed to create an item.
A progression requirement from Tier I through Tier V that limits access to more advanced recipes.
The Forge, Workbench, Alchemy Kit, Enchanting Table, or other facility required to perform a recipe.
A special crafting facility required by certain Tier V recipes. Possessing LT155 Eternal Forge Ember may also be required.
A standardized game state listed in the Status Effects database and identified by SE###.
A negative Status generally removed by recovery, cure, movement, or control-breaking effects.
A positive Status that improves offense, defense, recovery, movement, or utility.
A rules state used for movement forms, AI behavior, Equipment state, Quest state, or Campaign tracking.
A Hero Standard Action that normally costs 1 Action and moves the Hero to one adjacent connected revealed Location. Specific effects may grant a Move Action without spending an Action.

Leaving this Location voluntarily requires 1 additional unit of movement. A Hero must use 2 Move Actions to leave instead of 1; the first is spent overcoming the terrain and the second completes the move. An Enemy spends 1 additional Movement to leave. Forced Movement ignores this unless stated otherwise.
The next Attack against the affected Enemy gains +1 Attack; then remove Exposed.
A Hero-specific state with no inherent effect; cards that reference Stealth define its benefits and removal.

systemRules.name: System 001 — Hero Actions
systemRules.text: Each Hero gains 3 Actions at the start of their turn. Standard Actions include Move, Explore, Attack, Play Card, Interact, Rest, and Trade. A Hero may end their turn with Actions remaining; those Actions remain available for valid Reactions and effects until the End Phase. After all End Phase effects and Reactions resolve, all remaining unused Actions are lost.

systemRules.name: System 002 — Movement & Engagement
systemRules.text: A Hero Move is a Standard Action costing 1 Action and normally travels to one adjacent connected revealed Location. Resolve Leaving effects, move, then Entering effects. Engaged Heroes cannot voluntarily Move unless an effect allows it. Difficult Terrain: voluntarily leaving a Difficult Terrain Location requires 1 additional unit of movement. For a Hero, this means 1 additional Move Action; the first Move Action is spent overcoming the terrain and the second Move Action completes the move. For an Enemy, leaving Difficult Terrain costs 1 additional Movement. Forced Movement does not spend Actions and ignores Difficult Terrain unless the effect states otherwise. Special Movement such as Teleport, Blink, or Ethereal Movement follows its own text.

systemRules.name: System 004 — Combat
systemRules.text: Choose a valid target. Hero Attacks automatically hit and do not roll 1d6. Hero Attack Value = Hero Attack + Weapon Bonus + applicable modifiers. Damage = Hero Attack Value − Enemy Armor (minimum 1 for a normally resolving Attack unless an effect explicitly prevents, negates, cancels, or reduces Damage to 0). Resolve damage, defeat, and triggered effects.

systemRules.name: Round Structure
systemRules.text: Hero Phase → World Phase → End Phase. Each Hero completes Start of Turn, Draw, Gain 3 Actions, Perform Actions, End of Turn. Enemies then activate during World Phase.

systemRules.name: Enemy Activation
systemRules.text: Start → status check → determine target via Behavior Profile → movement → attack → special abilities → end.

systemRules.name: Hero Decks
systemRules.text: Each Hero begins with a unique 30-card deck; starting hand 5; draw 2 at start of turn; no maximum hand size; reshuffle discard when deck is empty.

systemRules.name: Equipment
systemRules.text: Equipment is separate from Hero Decks and remains equipped until replaced/removed. Current designed set includes EQ001–EQ120 across Weapons, Armor, Accessories, and legacy Shields.

systemRules.name: Campaign Formula
systemRules.text: 1 Campaign → 4 persistent World Events/chapters → 3 quests available per chapter → complete any 2 to advance (unless chapter states otherwise) → final chapter resolves finale and aftermath.

systemRules.name: Quest Rule
systemRules.text: Quest cards are scenario recipes. They should reference existing Location and Enemy card IDs rather than inventing new Locations during setup.

systemRules.name: Design Constraint
systemRules.text: Campaign 1 uses Location cards and N/E/S/W connection availability; no tactical grid or measured-space movement.

systemRules.name: Combat
systemRules.text: Hero Attack Value = Hero Attack + Weapon Bonus + applicable modifiers

systemRules.name: Combat
systemRules.text: Attacks automatically hit; no hit-roll modifier is used.

systemRules.name: Combat
systemRules.text: Hero Damage = Hero Attack Value − Enemy Armor. A normally resolving Attack deals a minimum of 1 Damage unless an effect explicitly prevents, negates, cancels, or reduces Damage to 0.

systemRules.name: Combat
systemRules.text: Heroes do not normally roll an Attack Die. When using an equipped Weapon, add that Weapon's Attack Bonus to the Hero's Attack Value.

systemRules.name: Combat
systemRules.text: Armor is the stat that reduces incoming Attack damage.

systemRules.name: Travel Encounter Deck
systemRules.text: When a Travel Encounter is triggered, draw the top Encounter card and roll 1d6 plus current World Event modifiers. Resolve the matching Severity band: 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, or 7+. After resolution, discard the card unless its text creates an ongoing effect.

systemRules.name: Travel Encounter Scaling
systemRules.text: World Event modifiers change the Encounter Severity roll. WE001 adds +1; WE002 replaces one normal Goblin with an Elite whenever possible; WE003 may add siege/pressure effects as printed; WE004 has no random Travel Encounters.

systemRules.name: Encounter Deck Reshuffle
systemRules.text: If the Encounter Deck is empty when a Travel Encounter is required, shuffle the Encounter discard pile to create a new Encounter Deck.

systemRules.name: Explore Action
systemRules.text: A Hero may spend 1 Action to Explore while occupying a revealed Location, unless a rule prevents it. Exploring draws and resolves the top valid card of the Exploration Deck.

systemRules.name: Explore — Other Triggers
systemRules.text: Cards, abilities, Quests, Locations, and other game effects may instruct a Hero to Explore. If the effect does not state an Action cost, the Explore occurs without spending an Action.

systemRules.name: Exploration Terrain
systemRules.text: When an Exploration card is drawn, resolve it if its Terrain is Any, Any Outdoor, or matches the current Location's Terrain, Traits, Keywords, or Location Type. Otherwise discard it and draw again until a valid card is found.

systemRules.name: Exploration Deck Reshuffle
systemRules.text: After an Exploration card resolves, discard it unless its text says to Keep it or place it elsewhere. If the Exploration Deck is empty when an Explore is required, shuffle its discard pile to create a new deck.

systemRules.name: Loot Deck
systemRules.text: When a rule instructs a Hero to draw Loot, draw from the Loot Deck unless a specific category/tag is named. Loot is added to that Hero's Inventory unless its card resolves immediately.

systemRules.name: Consumable Loot
systemRules.text: Consumable Loot remains in a Hero's Inventory until used. Resolve the printed Effect, then discard the Loot card unless it specifically remains in play.

systemRules.name: Gold
systemRules.text: Gold is tracked as a campaign resource and is not represented by Loot cards. Effects that grant Gold add it directly to the party/Hero total as defined by campaign bookkeeping.

systemRules.name: Quest Item Loot
systemRules.text: Quest Items are persistent story objects. They cannot be voluntarily sold or discarded unless a Quest, Campaign rule, or the Item itself specifically allows it.

systemRules.name: Relic Loot
systemRules.text: Relics are unique persistent treasures with ongoing or limited-use effects. Unless stated otherwise, a Relic is not Equipment and does not occupy a normal Equipment slot.

systemRules.name: Legendary Treasure
systemRules.text: Legendary Treasures are unique Campaign rewards. Their effects, unlocks, or record requirements persist according to their card and Campaign text.

systemRules.name: Crafting
systemRules.text: A Hero may craft only when a Location, Scenario, or Campaign rule provides access to the Required Tool listed on the recipe. Pay all listed Materials and Gold, then resolve the recipe.

systemRules.name: Crafting Materials
systemRules.text: Required Materials are discarded from Inventory when crafting begins unless a recipe specifically states that a component is not consumed.

systemRules.name: Crafting Tiers
systemRules.text: Tier I recipes are basic; Tier II–IV require the listed Crafting Tier or equivalent Campaign unlock; Tier V recipes are Legendary and also require all printed unlock conditions.

systemRules.name: Craft Time
systemRules.text: Craft Time is paid in Actions when crafting during a Scenario. Between Scenarios, the Campaign may allow crafting without spending Scenario Actions, but all Materials, Gold, Tools, and unlocks are still required.

systemRules.name: Crafted Results
systemRules.text: When a recipe is completed, gain the Result ID named on the recipe. Equipment enters Inventory unequipped; Loot enters Inventory unless its own rules state otherwise.

systemRules.name: Heroes advance by replacing their current Hero card with a higher-level Hero card. Each Hero card is a complete representation of that hero at that level; no separate Hero Progression database is used.
Status Effects
systemRules.text: Status Effects are standardized temporary, persistent, equipment, enemy-state, Quest-state, or Campaign-state rules identified by SE###.

systemRules.name: Applying Status Effects
systemRules.text: When an effect applies a Status Effect, place the corresponding marker or record it on the affected game element. Apply its Effect immediately unless stated otherwise.

systemRules.name: Status Duration
systemRules.text: A Status remains until its listed Duration ends or its Removal condition is satisfied. Removing a Status immediately ends all of its effects.

systemRules.name: Status Stacking
systemRules.text: Unless Stacks says Yes, a unit cannot have multiple instances of the same Status. Reapplying a non-stacking Status refreshes its Duration but does not multiply its effect.

systemRules.name: Status Conflicts
systemRules.text: If two Status Effects modify the same value, apply both unless one specifically prevents the other. Immunity prevents the Status from being applied.

systemRules.name: Status References
systemRules.text: Cards may reference either the Status Name or Status ID. The Status Effects sheet is the source of truth for the full definition.

systemRules.name: Hero-Created Tokens — General
systemRules.text: Hero-created tokens belong to the Hero that created them. They are not Heroes or Enemies, do not take turns or Actions, and only Move, Attack, deal damage, or trigger effects when a Hero ability/card explicitly says so. Unless a specific rule says otherwise, remove all Hero-created tokens when the encounter ends.

systemRules.name: Bone Servant
systemRules.text: Bone Servants are Summoned tokens controlled by Mordren. They have no Health or Armor, cannot be targeted by Attacks, and do not activate independently. They exist only to satisfy and resolve Mordren effects. Mordren's maximum is 1 at Level 1, 2 at Levels 2–3, and 3 at Levels 4–6. If an effect would place a Servant above the maximum, do not place the excess token. A removed Servant leaves play.

systemRules.name: Spirit Totem
systemRules.text: Spirit Totems are non-unit tokens controlled by Asha. They have no Health or Armor, cannot be targeted by Attacks, and do not activate independently. Asha may have 1 Spirit Totem in play at Levels 1–3 and up to 2 at Levels 4–6. Grand Totem may temporarily exceed this maximum by 1 as printed. If Asha is above her normal maximum when Grand Totem's effect ends, remove one of her Spirit Totems. Remove all Spirit Totems when the encounter ends.

systemRules.name: Turret
systemRules.text: A Turret is a stationary Construct controlled by Mira with 4 Health and 1 Armor. It cannot Move and does not activate independently. Once during each of Mira's turns, it may deal 2 damage to one Enemy in its Location as stated by Deploy Turret. Enemy Attacks and effects that can target a Construct may target it. At 0 Health it is Defeated and removed. Mira may have only one Turret in play unless an effect says otherwise. Remove it when the encounter ends.

systemRules.name: Spirit Wolf
systemRules.text: A Spirit Wolf is a Summoned unit controlled by Thorne with 3 Health and 0 Armor. It does not activate or Move independently unless another effect says so. Enemy Attacks and effects may target it. At 0 Health it is Defeated and removed. Thorne may have only one Spirit Wolf in play; placing another removes the previous Spirit Wolf. Remove it when the encounter ends.

systemRules.name: Unarmed — Kael Windstep
systemRules.text: Kael's Unarmed attacks count as a Melee Weapon with +2 Weapon Bonus for his Basic Attacks and Hero cards that use his normal Attack. Unarmed occupies Kael's Weapon slot but is not an Equipment card and cannot be discarded, traded, or unequipped. If an effect specifically equips Kael with another Weapon, use that Weapon's rules instead.

systemRules.name: Mana Terminology
systemRules.text: Ascendance has no Mana resource or Mana-cost system. 'Mana' may appear in thematic proper names such as Mana Burn or Mana Crystal, but those names do not create or spend a Mana resource. Arcane cards and Equipment use the normal Action economy unless their text explicitly says otherwise.

systemRules.name: Quest Hero-Count Scaling
systemRules.text: Quest enemy setups use the printed Quest text as the 2-Hero baseline. Apply the Quest sheet's Hero-Count Scaling column for 1, 3, or 4 Heroes. Scaling adds or removes ordinary enemies and reinforcement pressure; named bosses, unique objectives, objective Health, and victory/defeat thresholds do not scale unless the Quest explicitly says they do. Never duplicate a named Boss/Legendary enemy solely because Hero count increases.

systemRules.name: Travel Encounter Hero-Count Scaling
systemRules.text: After resolving the Encounter card's Severity band, adjust combat bodies for party size: 1 Hero — remove 1 ordinary non-Elite/non-Boss Enemy if the band contains 2 or more Enemies (minimum 1 Enemy). 2 Heroes — no change. 3 Heroes — add 1 ordinary Enemy matching a normal Enemy already listed. 4 Heroes — add 2 ordinary Enemies matching normal Enemies already listed, or add 1 ordinary Enemy if the band already contains a Boss. Do not duplicate Bosses or Legendary Enemies through this rule. Hazard/Story/Discovery encounters without combat are unchanged.

systemRules.name: Party Gold & Treasury
systemRules.status: Unless a specific effect names a Hero, all Gold gained from Quests, Loot, Search, Encounters, Campaign effects, selling, or other rewards is added once to the shared Party Treasury. Costs are paid from that Treasury. Quest Gold is a single party reward, never separate Gold per Hero. When a Quest awards a numeric Gold amount, apply Party-Size Gold Scaling once to that reward.

systemRules.name: Merchant Pricing
systemRules.status: A merchant buys eligible Equipment, Loot, Trade Goods, and Crafting Materials for 50% of their numeric listed Value, rounded down to the nearest 5 Gold (minimum 0). A merchant sells at listed Value unless a World Event, Reputation effect, Campaign rule, or other specific effect modifies the price. Priceless, Artifact, Quest Item, and 0-Value items cannot normally be sold.

systemRules.name: Crafting Professions
systemRules.status: The four standard Professions are Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Enchanting, and Artificing. Crafting progression is tracked by Profession, not by World Event, Quest number, or Campaign chapter. This allows the same crafting rules to function across multiple Campaigns.

systemRules.name: Profession Mastery
systemRules.status: Each Profession has a party Mastery total. When the party completes at least one recipe from a Profession during a Downtime period, gain 1 Mastery in that Profession after Downtime ends. A Profession can gain at most 1 Mastery per Downtime, regardless of how many recipes are completed. Mastery is persistent Campaign progression and is recorded in the Campaign save.

systemRules.name: Crafting Tier Unlocks
systemRules.status: Tier I is always unlocked. Tier II unlocks at 2 Mastery, Tier III at 4 Mastery, Tier IV at 7 Mastery, and Tier V at 10 Mastery in that Profession. A recipe may be crafted only if its Profession has unlocked that recipe's Tier and all other printed requirements are satisfied. Specific rewards may unlock a Tier earlier.

systemRules.name: Downtime Crafting
systemRules.status: Crafting is performed during Downtime unless a specific effect permits crafting during a Scenario. Pay the recipe's listed Gold Cost from the Party Treasury, spend the listed materials, satisfy the Required Tool and Unlock Requirement, then gain the listed Result. Craft Time is used only when an effect creates a limited Downtime Action budget; otherwise it is descriptive of recipe effort and does not consume Hero combat Actions.

systemRules.name: Crafting Economy Principle
systemRules.status: Listed item Value is a merchant/reference value, not a requirement that a recipe's ingredients plus Gold equal that Value. Crafting is intentionally allowed to create value from gathered materials. The Merchant Pricing rule prevents routine buy-craft-sell loops: purchased inputs are paid at full listed Value while crafted outputs sell for only half listed Value.

systemRules.name: Final Quest / World Event Reward Precedence
systemRules.status: When a Final Quest both completes a World Event and ends a Campaign, resolve the Final Quest rewards first. The World Event then grants only rewards that are explicitly additional. If the Final Quest and World Event list the same tangible reward category for the same victory milestone, do not duplicate it unless the World Event explicitly states 'in addition to the Final Quest rewards.'

systemRules.name: Auto-Hit Equipment Wording
systemRules.status: Equipment must not rely on Hero attack rolls, misses, or critical-hit ranges unless a specific effect explicitly creates such a roll. Hero Attacks automatically hit under System 004. Equipment may instead trigger when an Attack is declared, resolves, deals Damage, defeats a target, or meets another observable game state.

systemRules.name: Party-Size Gold Scaling
systemRules.status: Apply this multiplier once to numeric Quest Gold before adding it to the Party Treasury: 1 Hero ×0.75; 2 Heroes ×1.00; 3 Heroes ×1.25; 4 Heroes ×1.50. Round the final Quest Gold reward to the nearest 5 Gold. This is one shared party payout, not Gold per Hero. Search, Loot, Encounter, selling, and fixed non-Quest Gold are not multiplied unless their effect explicitly says otherwise.

systemRules.name: Economy Scaling Principle
systemRules.status: Party-size Gold scaling is intentionally sublinear. Additional Heroes create additional Equipment demand, but they also bring complete starting Equipment and increase the party's combat capacity. The rule increases upgrade purchasing power without multiplying the economy directly by Hero count.

systemRules.name: Party-Size Equipment Reward Scaling
systemRules.status: When a Quest or World Event awards exactly 1 Equipment Card to the party, draw/gain 1 Equipment Card for a 1–2 Hero party and 2 Equipment Cards for a 3–4 Hero party. Preserve the printed rarity requirement for every card gained. Rewards that already say 'per Hero' are not multiplied by this rule. Starting Equipment, Search draws, Loot effects, merchant purchases, and crafting results are unchanged unless their own effect says otherwise.

systemRules.name: Campaign Progression Target
systemRules.status: Campaign 1 is not required to bring every Hero to maximum Level on the required-only route. Optional Quests and all-Quest World Event bonuses are intended to accelerate progression. The required-only route ends at 1700 XP (Level 5); completing all Quests and WE001–WE003 bonuses reaches 2225 XP (Level 6 before the separate WE004 victory record).

systemRules.name: Regional Campaign Hubs
systemRules.status: Major settlements and cities may function as persistent Campaign Hubs. Hubs may provide merchants, factions, recovery, crafting access, information, and region-specific services. Hub rules modify access and availability but do not replace universal Equipment, Loot, Crafting, Profession, or Reputation systems.

systemRules.name: Campaign Bands & Standalone Entry
systemRules.status: Campaigns are not required to form one mandatory linear Level chain. A Campaign may define a recommended entry Level and a standalone entry package. Continuing Heroes preserve legal persistent progression; standalone Heroes use the package defined by that Campaign.

systemRules.name: Regional Location Pools
systemRules.status: Region tags organize the world and reusable content, but an active Quest still defines the exact Quest Location Pool and Quest Location Stack. A Region does not automatically add all of its Locations to a Quest.

systemRules.name: Campaign II — Shadows Over Valewatch
systemRules.status: Campaign II uses WE005–WE008 and Q013–Q024 in the Crownlands/Valewatch region. It is a Veteran-band Campaign beginning around Level 5–6 and may advance Heroes through authored Level 7 and Level 8 progression. The v10.37 standalone Level-5 equivalency package remains valid. Status: Playtest; not print-lock until digital/physical campaign playtests validate the curve.

systemRules.name: Hero Progression Through Level 16
systemRules.status: Hero progression is authored through Level 16. L9 4400, L10 5400, L11 6500, L12 7700, L13 9000, L14 10400, L15 11900, L16 13500.

systemRules.name: Campaign II Standalone Entry Package
systemRules.status: To begin Shadows Over Valewatch without Campaign I: each Hero begins at Level 5 with 1400 XP and their authored Level-5 Hero state/deck; keep normal starting Equipment, then gain 1 compatible Rare Equipment, 1 compatible Epic Equipment, and 1 compatible Legendary Equipment per Hero (redraw an incompatible random result); grant the Party Treasury 100 Gold per participating Hero; set one chosen Profession to 2 Mastery and a second chosen Profession to 1 Mastery; all other Profession Mastery begins at 0. Normal one-time starting Healing Potion rules still apply. This is the v10.37 playtest equivalency package, not a universal Campaign rule.

systemRules.name: Current Hero Level Cap / Banked XP
systemRules.status: Level 16 at 13500 XP is the current highest authored Hero Level and initial six-campaign saga cap. XP above 13500 is banked until future progression is authored.

systemRules.name: Campaign III — Heart of the Mountain
systemRules.status: Campaign III uses WE009–WE012 and Q025–Q036 in the Ironspine Mountains/Ironhaven region. Its signature persistent system is Mountain Stability (Instability 0–8), which may alter routes, hazards, setup pressure, hub state, and finale conditions. Stability must remain recoverable and cannot make required Quests unwinnable before players can respond.

systemRules.name: Campaign III Standalone Entry Principle
systemRules.status: First-pass standalone target is Level 7 / 2700 XP. The exact Ironhaven Equipment, Gold, consumable, and Profession equivalency package will be set during the detailed Campaign III balance pass; it must not assume prior Campaign completion.

systemRules.name: Mountain Stability — Campaign III
systemRules.status: Campaign III tracks Instability from 0–8 and begins at 2. Stable 0–2 has no global penalty. Fractured 3–5 strengthens the first structural Hazard each Quest. Critical 6–7 also gives +1 Health to the first scripted non-Boss Construct/Deep Creature group each Quest. Track 8 causes Quest-specific Collapse consequences rather than automatic campaign defeat.

systemRules.name: Ironspine Regional Encounter Deck
systemRules.status: Campaign III uses EN046–EN060 as its regional Travel Encounter deck. WE009 currently authors EN046–EN050. Ironspine Quests should not draw Valewatch/Goblin regional encounters unless a Quest explicitly imports them.

systemRules.name: Campaign III Standalone Entry Package
systemRules.status: Standalone Heart of the Mountain starts each Hero at Level 7 / 2700 XP with normal starting Equipment plus 1 compatible Rare, 1 Epic, and 1 Legendary Equipment; 150 Gold per Hero in Party Treasury; one Profession at 3 Mastery and a second at 2; normal starting consumables.

systemRules.name: Campaign III — Full Authored Range
systemRules.status: Heart of the Mountain now uses WE009–WE012, Q025–Q036, L088–L124, E051–E068, EN046–EN060, and LT167–LT172. All Campaign III content is Playtest pending live evidence.

systemRules.name: Campaign III Progression Target
systemRules.status: Standalone required-only Campaign III contributes 1700 XP and ends at 4400 XP / Level 9. Standalone completionist contributes 2525 XP and ends at 5225 XP, 175 short of Level 10. Strong continuation/completionist profiles may reach Level 10 during Campaign III.

systemRules.name: Campaign III Finale State
systemRules.status: Q036 uses final Instability, saved Ironhaven facilities, Emberdeep Alliance, Heartstone Harmonized, Fast Descent, and Campaign III Quest Items to alter setup. Optional aids may reduce pressure but are not required for victory.

systemRules.name: Campaign IV — The Withering Wilds
systemRules.status: Campaign IV uses WE013–WE016, Q037–Q048, L125–L161, E069–E087, EN061–EN075, and LT173–LT178 in the Verdant Reach / Eldergrove region. Status: Playtest.

systemRules.name: Blight — Campaign IV
systemRules.status: Campaign IV tracks Blight 0–8 starting at 2. 0–2 has no global penalty; 3–5 strengthens the first Blight/Poison/Spore Hazard each Quest; 6–7 also grants +1 Health to the first eligible scripted non-Boss Blighted/Plant/Spirit group; 8 causes Quest-specific Rot Crisis, not automatic Campaign defeat.

systemRules.name: Campaign IV Standalone Entry Package
systemRules.status: Standalone The Withering Wilds starts at Level 9 / 4400 XP with normal starting Equipment plus 1 compatible Rare, 1 Epic, 1 Legendary, and 1 Mythic-compatible Equipment per Hero; 200 Gold per Hero; one Profession at 4 Mastery and a second at 3; normal starting consumables.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Party Shared
systemRules.status: Reputation is tracked per campaign party/world state, not per Hero. Each named faction plus General Reputation has a score from -5 to +6. Scores persist and synchronize through the authoritative campaign save.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Standing Thresholds
systemRules.status: -5 to -3 Hostile; -2 to -1 Distrusted; 0 Neutral; 1–2 Friendly; 3–4 Trusted; 5–6 Exalted. Higher tiers retain lower-tier perks unless explicitly stated otherwise.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Regional Scope
systemRules.status: Named-faction perks normally function only in their home region. General Reputation can function across regions. Reputation cannot make a required Quest unwinnable.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Resolution
systemRules.status: Reputation gains/losses apply exactly once when a Quest or World Event resolution commits. Digital implementation must be idempotent and room/server authoritative, including once-per-Quest perk consumption.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Campaign I Legacy
systemRules.status: Any older Campaign I reward or penalty that says only 'Reputation' is interpreted as General Reputation. This changes wording, not reward magnitude.

systemRules.name: Faction Reputation — Perk Source
systemRules.status: The Faction Reputation sheet is the source of truth for Friendly, Trusted, Exalted, Distrusted, and Hostile benefits/pressures for General, Stonebrook, Crownlands, Ironspine, and Verdant Reach factions.

systemRules.name: Campaign V — The Drowned Tide
systemRules.status: Campaign V uses WE017–WE020, Q049–Q060, L162–L198, E088–E106, EN076–EN090, LT179–LT184, Ashenport, and Doomtide 0–8. Status: Playtest.

systemRules.name: Doomtide — Campaign V
systemRules.status: Campaign V begins Doomtide 2. 0–2 no global penalty; 3–5 strengthens first Flood/Current/Storm Hazard; 6–7 also grants +1 Health to first eligible scripted non-Boss Drowned/Sea group; 8 uses Quest-specific Black Tide crisis.

systemRules.name: Campaign VI — Crown of the Fallen Sun
systemRules.status: Campaign VI uses WE021–WE024, Q061–Q072, L199–L235, E107–E125, EN091–EN105, LT185–LT190, Sunspire, and Sunfall 0–8. Status: Playtest.

systemRules.name: Sunfall — Campaign VI
systemRules.status: Campaign VI begins Sunfall 2. 0–2 no global penalty; 3–5 strengthens first Heat/Mirage/Solar Hazard; 6–7 also grants +1 Health to first eligible scripted non-Boss Solar/Construct/Undead group; 8 uses Quest-specific Black Sun crisis.

systemRules.name: Initial Six-Campaign Saga
systemRules.status: Campaigns I–VI now form the authored initial world saga. Campaigns remain individually playable with standalone entry packages; linear completion is not mandatory. Q072 is the saga finale but does not invalidate future expansions.
